products.name: Krita AI
products.note: Open-source digital art; local AI plugins; no cloud dependency; community governance

reading.body:
Krita Foundation operates a free, community-governed digital art tool with local AI plugins that require no cloud infrastructure, keeping computation and data on user hardware.

The foundation's model inverts the typical AI software economics. Rather than centralizing compute on remote servers to capture user data and lock in switching costs, Krita pushes inference to the edge. This trades away the ability to scale a large training dataset from user interactions, but it eliminates the power and cooling burden that would otherwise fall on the foundation's infrastructure budget. For users, it means no dependency on external API availability or cloud pricing.

The local-first approach also reflects genuine constraints on the foundation's resource base. As a nonprofit operating on community contributions rather than venture capital or advertising revenue, Krita cannot sustain the data center footprint that would be necessary to serve millions of concurrent users remotely. The plugin architecture allows contributors to add AI capability without the foundation bearing the full operational cost.

This does not mean Krita competes with cloud-native AI design tools on raw capability. Local inference on consumer hardware operates under different performance ceilings than server-grade compute. The data provided does not specify which models the plugins run, their size, speed, or accuracy relative to alternatives. It confirms only that the foundation has chosen the architectural path that matches its nonprofit structure and community values.

profile_text.body:
The Krita Foundation is a nonprofit, open-source foundation that develops and maintains Krita, a digital painting and image editing application. The foundation operates under community governance and makes its software freely available, with no reliance on cloud-based infrastructure.

On the AI side, the foundation offers Krita AI, an open-source digital art tool that supports local AI plugins, meaning AI functionality runs on the user's own hardware rather than through external cloud services. The project's community governance model means development priorities and direction are shaped collectively rather than by a corporate owner.

The held facts carry no litigation, patent filings, MCP server registrations, or SEC records associated with the Krita Foundation, consistent with its status as a nonprofit open-source organization.
